steps.say: Shunts drain water to the belly through a pressure valve. Entry point, valve choice and trajectory decide a decade of trouble-free drainage.
steps.tx: **Ventriculoperitoneal shunting** (brain to belly tube) through the **Kocher point** (skull entry mark) or Keen entry remains first-line for **communicating hydrocephalus** (absorption failure dropsy), with **programmable valves** (adjustable pressure gates) allowing transcutaneous pressure adjustment without revision surgery, plus neuronavigation guiding difficult ventricular cannulation.

steps.say: A hole in the third ventricle floor bypasses blocks without hardware. The basilar artery underneath demands respect.
steps.tx: **Endoscopic third ventriculostomy** (keyhole **3rd ventricle** floor hole) fenestrates the tuber cinereum floor anterior to the mammillary bodies and posterior to the infundibulum, demanding respect for the **basilar tip** (base artery end) below, with Doppler checking flow after the stoma opens and Liliequist membrane fenestration completing the passage.

steps.say: A score predicts who stays shunt-free after the hole. Older children with virgin aqueduct blocks do best.
steps.tx: The **ETV success score** (hole success scale) combines age, aetiology and prior shunt history, predicting durable success best in older children with **aqueduct stenosis** (narrow channel block) or tectal tumours and no prior shunt, while infants with post-infective blocks score lowest.

steps.say: Blocked tubes announce themselves differently at each end. Headache up top, belly pain below.
steps.tx: **Proximal obstruction** (head end block) from choroid or debris is commonest, presenting with headache, vomiting and a flat slow-refill reservoir, while **distal failure** (belly end block) presents with abdominal **pseudocyst** (fluid pocket) or peritonitis needing shunt series imaging, with plain films tracing the whole catheter course.

steps.say: Infected hardware always comes out. Antibiotics alone through plastic never sterilise a biofilm.
steps.tx: **Shunt infection** (tube germ seeding), usually **Staph epidermidis** (skin germ) within **6 months** (six months) of surgery, needs complete hardware removal with **external drainage** (outside tube) plus antibiotics, never antibiotics alone through an infected shunt, with vancomycin plus cefepime as typical empiric cover.

steps.say: Overdrainage sucks the brain down. Slit ventricles and blood collections mean the valve setting is too low.
steps.tx: **Overdrainage** (excess siphoning) causes **slit-ventricle syndrome** (squeezed chambers), subdural collections and postural headache, managed by upgrading to programmable or **anti-siphon valves** (gravity guards) rather than repeated shunt ligation operations, with symptomatic collections washed out and headaches charted against valve changes.

steps.say: Back shunts dodge the head but invite sinking brains. Pressure dissociation pulls the tonsils down.
steps.tx: **Lumboperitoneal shunts** (spine to belly tubes) suit communicating hydrocephalus and idiopathic intracranial hypertension but risk acquired **Chiari** (tonsil descent) from craniospinal **pressure dissociation** (head-spine gap), so ventricles are checked serially with positional headache diaries and valve upgrades preferred over repeated ligations.

steps.say: Shunt dependence is lifelong. Blocked tubes kill in hours, so every family carries a drill card and a valve record.
steps.tx: **Shunt dependence** (tube reliance) is never assumed away: a blocked shunt in a shunt-dependent adult is lethal within hours, so emergency **drill cards** (action slips), valve settings records and **24 hour neurosurgical access** (day-night cover) are counselled at every single visit.
